title: Shore blocking for well-foundedness: an infinite descending sequence below the natural product of the ordinal bound with k
author: Quentin Le Houérou; Ludovic Levy Patey; Keita Yokoyama
work: Conservation of Ramsey's theorem for pairs and well-foundedness
difficulty_reason: The counted unit is the lemma labelled lem:shore-blocking-wf at source lines 426-431: from any failure of well-foundedness below an ordinal beta witnessed by one of finitely many Turing functionals, it builds a single Turing functional Gamma-sub-k whose output is an M-infinite decreasing sequence below the natural product beta times k, with an index computable in k. The work is concentrated in the second half of the proof: the functionals are first twisted so that convergence at an input forces convergence at every smaller input and a strictly decreasing run of values below beta (source lines 434-439), and only then can the measurement alpha(sigma,e) be defined as the last convergent value and proved monotone in the oracle segment (source line 441). The blocking functional searches beyond the length of the previously found segment rather than beyond the previous input, which is what makes the newly found value strictly smaller than the old one (source lines 443-444 and 448-449); the natural sum of the k measurements is what converts k separate partial failures into one sequence, and the natural product bound beta times k is exactly what the companion lemma lem:wf-product needs. Totality of the blocking functional is not free either: it comes from totality of a single Phi-sub-e to the X plus the induction scheme for Sigma-0-1 formulas available in the model (source lines 446-447).
